Back In 1851, in the midst of a
shooting war in Korea, the United
Nations at United States insistence
adopted a resolution calling for an
embargo on trade with Communist
China. The clamp-down involved
not only military supplies and
equipment but q long list of items
which might conceivably aid Pei
pings economy, thus indirectly
strengthening her war machine.
At the time. Communist Chinese
volunteers" were battling United
Nations troops in Korea. and the
Red regime of Mao Tse-tung. had
been officially declared an aggressor.
There was little objection among
Western nations against the trade
limitations. although the British,
additionally heavy traders with
China, were unenthusiastic.


But since the 1858 armistice with
the Communists ended the shooting
in Korea, the British and to a lesser
extent other European nations have
grown FESTIVE under the ban. In
creasingly, the British crown colony
Of Hong Kong has become center
for bootleg" commerce with Red
China-not. Of course. with Lon
don's sanction but with the
tacit approval Of shipping and
commercial interests of many
nationalities.


The reStiveness : was economic.
Britain, historically dependent on
her large export trade, needed the
big China market for the output of
her factories. Since the Communist
take-over in China in 1949, British
commercial and financial activities
there had almost vanished (see
story by Robert Jackson on page
A-26). But actual trade-on Pei
pings terms continued high until
the 1851 controls were applied.


Pressure mounted on the London
government for relaxing or out
right abandonment of the trade
barriers. At the Bermuda confer
ence last March, Prime Minister
Harold Macmillan and Foreign Sec
rotary Selwyn Lloyd pressed Presi-
dent Eisenhower and Secretary Of
State Dulles for American agree
ment to ease the restrictions. But
they found Mr.. Dulles determinedly
opposed. In the end. the British
leaders won only q grudging United
States acceptance of formal study
Of the problem by the NATO
powers.

The placement law was part

white schools are yet involved

Can Go to Court

Noise haraSsed residents of North
Arlington and Georgetown will welcome
the relief from airplane din promised
by the Civil Aeronautics Administration.
They have been asking for relief for sew
eral years, as air traffic has increased
and the size, power and racket of air.
liners have grown apace. In response
to the appeals, flight paths have been
altered and various rules and instructions
issued-but the roar of low-fying air
planes over residential sections on both
sides of the Potomac above Key Bridge
has continued. Now, however, new
plan for abating the noise nuisance has
been adopted.


The plan involves the installation
near Chain Bridge of beacon light to
mark the turmoil point for airliners
leaving the Washington Airport for the
North and West. This bridge long ago
was designated as the point over the Po-
tomac River where commercial aircraft
should begin their break from the airport
take-off pattern, but many pilots either
do not know where the point is or dis
regard it. The Chain Bridge turmoil
point was selected in a move to keep
climbing airliners, with their laundering
engines, over the river until they are
past the thickly congested Arlington and
Georgetown areas and high enough to
reduce the noise at ground level


In the belief that most of the off,
river flying of which so many citizens
have complained has been due to pilot
confusion or forgetfulness, the CAA has
announced that a fixed signal light will
be placed in the vicinity of Chain Bridge
as a combination guide and warning to
flyers. This system at least will elm
mate excuses that uncertainty over the
exact turmoil place caused reported de-
viationS from the approved flight path.

OIlCe upon b JlttlS tLlcIO
was a pretty little county
nam ed Prince Backward
County. Like many pretty
counties. Prince Backward
Just couldn't help but grow.
Every year there were more
houses and more people. but
Prince Backwards growth
was lopsided. The roads
didn't grow-just the holes
in them. The FIRE depart
ments didn't grow-the old
engines just grew older.
Though the schools grew.
they didn't grow as fast as
the growing children.


Finally. one day when thu
kids were sitting three deep
at their school desks. the
exasperated citizens Of
Prince Backward squeezed
into their school house and
shouted: This has got to
stop!" They decided that
there were some things that
Prince Backward needed as
much as people and houses:
so miles Of smooth new
roads. for instance: 100 miles
Of nice big sewer pipes, and
a lot more handsome fire.
men and dashing cops. But
to pay for all this they had
to raise their tax rate to IS
per 500. Goodness graci-
ous." cried one fearful tax
payer. why should we have
to pay 500 more taxes than
the citizens Of Queen Forward
County?" Well. let's find
out why.


In the beginning, Queen
Forward County was no pref
tier than Prince Backward
County. The dogwood didn't
bloom any brighter and the
cardinals didn't sing any
louder, but when Queen For
ward started to grow. all of
it grew together. Not Just
the people and houses-;he
fire department. police de-
partment. road department
and school department. They
all grew together and the
kids had plenty Of room to
study. The citizens were
never exasperated like the
citizens Of Prince Backward
and there wasn't one ulcer to
be found in the whole county.
That was because the tax
rate was cnly $2.70 per 500,
nearly 500 less than the rate
in Prince Backward. The
reason Prince Backward grew
wrong and Queen Fol ward
grew right-the reason Prince
Backward citizens had to pay
so much more taxes and have
so little to show for their
money is industry.


Prince Backward citizens
were frightened by industry
and they discouraged indus
try from locating there.
Queen Forward citizens,
however. welcomed selective
industry from the very first.
Every 100 industrial employees
gave Queen Forward $500, 900
more personal income per
year. $270.000 more bank de-
posits. "a more jobs outside
the industry. 4 more retail
establishments and $3.50, 900
more retail sales per year
Most of all. Queen Forward
County citizens liked the way
industry helped foot the tax
bill and improve all sorts of
municipal facilities. Prince
Backward citizens didn't
want industry because they
said 1t was noisy. or dirty, or
would pollute the air. But
Queen Forward County citi-
zens. who grew up with in
dustry, pointed out: Their air
was as sweet smelling as a
rose: their county was as
clean as a whistle. The secret
Of Queen Forwards growth
was controlled development.
Population and industry ex-
panued together, each help
ing the other.


Controlled development
consists Of overall planning
that puts industries where
they belong and residential
areas where they belong, so
that neither will interfere
with the other. Counties that
have grown without industry
and now want 1t to help pay
skyrocketing taxes, often find
that 1t is too late because un-
controlled residential expan-
sion left no room for plant
sites.


Let's make a balanced
growth in industry and
homes through controlled de-
velopment. We in Fairfax
County should adopt the slo-
gan Lets broaden the tax
base, don't raise the tax"


william G. Sims,


Chairman, Economic and


Industrial Development


Committee Of Fairfax


County.

SALEM, Oreg.-More travellers
seeking to get that healthy glow
from a vacation in the rugged
mountains are trying the pack
horse civilization" Of Northeast
ern Oregon.


Some luxuries are available,
but for the most part the va.
cationer will drive over mountain
passes. through forest corridors,
then hike or ride a horse, or drive
over dirt and gravel forest serv-
ice roads to choice recreational
areas.


Primitive Area


Take, for instance, the Wallowa
Mountains. into which no road
penetrates. The mountains,
centered in a national forest, sur.
round numerous lakes and give
birth to many streams, and are
accessible only by pack horse.
For those who like the primitive
life. this area is unrivaled.


Lakes and streams TEEN with
fighting trout. and hunters sell
dom fail to down q deer. Well
over half Of them are able to
bring an elk to the dinner table.
for the Wallowas contain the
largest supply Of elk in the
United States.


For Others, Too


But Northeastern Oregon is
not for sportsmen alone. Parks,
forest camps and picnic areas
help to make the area pleasant
for sightseers. Notable among
these is Wallowa State Park at
Wallowa Lake. Horses for pack
trips into the Wallowas may be
obtained at the rustic lodge here.


Northeastern Oregon also con-
tains the deepest chasm on the
North American Continent, the
Grand Canyon Of the Snake
River. 1000 feet deeper than the
Grand Canyon Of the Colorado.
"A forest service road leads trav-
elers to the closest accessible spot
by car.

mites between Alexandria and Mount

ernmental agencies. including the Fed
eral Bureau of. Public Roads, the Ma

dria. But the chief responsibility for

bands that originated among Trinidad
hoodlums decade ago. Using garbage
can lids, metal oil drums and similar
scrap, the "robustmen" of those days
were fashioning the new technique in
defiance Of an island ban against over
exuberant musical orgies, and to cope
with wartime shortage of conventional
musical instruments. Only few years
ago the rivalry among the "tinpany"
bands had reached the stage OF gang
warfare, requiring establishment of a
commando police force and the good

savagery has been soothed and "tinpany"

commodity.

beaten into shapes that give a wide
range OF notes when played with rubber
headed drumsticks Still, who knows?

the "rock and roll" craze of our own
exuberant youth. And II not this, 1t could
at least provide some use for old garbage
can lids.

NEWPORT NEWS, Va. Jan.
16.-Four young daughters of
diplomats were back home in
Washington today after spend
ing the most exciting day of
their lives in this shipbuilding
city yesterday.


And now they may tell their
classmates they're assistant
shipwrights." For that was the
honorary title with which they
were dubbed when they made
local maritime history here
yesterday and lowered into
place the keel plate of the new
Grace Line passenger liner.
Santa Rosa"


The new assistant ship
wrights," who represented
countries the new liner will
serve. are Miss Elena Cervan-

Yesterdays temperatures in
this seaport were below freez-
ing. and the open wooden
platform on shipway where
the ceremony was held must
have been the coolest place
in town. At any rate. there
seemed to be an unspoken
agreement among the par
ticipating officials from New
York and Washington to keep
speeches to the minimum and
leave all the glory to the four
young ladies who provided the
climax to the historic drama.


AS a large crane swung
down with the keel assembly
and moved it toward the plat
form. the United States Air
Force Tactical Air Command
Band warmed things up"
with some South American
samba rhythms. Then, the
four girls took their places at
the four corners of the steel
box-like structure, on the
underside of which was the
keel plate.


Each of them held an old
fashioned bouquet of sweet
heart roses with long rose
streamers. Next, they each
were presented with a pair of
feminine looking calico plas-
tic "shipwright's gloves" and
asked to grab hold of the
chain hoists at the four
corners of the keel assembly.
Then came the signal to pull,
q resounding "clank." and the
laying of the keel plate Of the
new vessel was done.


Sets a Shipbuilding Precedent


Undersecretary of Commerce
Walter Williams was the prin-
cipal speaker at the ceremony,
which marked the first time
work has started on replace
ment of major vessel in OPP
Grafton under the same name

namesake is still in service).
The occasion also inaugurated
beginning of a 1885 million
fleet replacement program re-
sulting from an agreement
signed last January between
Grace Line and the Federal
Maritime Administration.

ment-backed morning paper
Alshaab reported from Beirut

strikes against its authority.

cheered when they entered the
cathedral.

strike in the capital and in

practice of granting discounts.

week ended March 9 trailed
year-ago business by 10 per cent.

means all--of the decline was
due to last years earlier Easter.
At this time last year Easter was
only a few weeks away.


Home builders for some time
now have been complaining
bitterly about the Governments
tight money" policy. But the
cloud was not without its silver
lining-builders were told in
Washington that the credit

The British Commonwealth, that
unique family Of nations, took on an
other member last week end with the
proclaimed independence Of the Fedora
ton Of Malaga. Under European infiu-
ence for more than four centuries and
under British control for most of the
time since 1855, the new nation Is born
In an atmosphere of political and eco
nomic uncertainty. It's population is
q mixture Of native Malayans, Chinese,
Indians and Pakistanis, plus smaller
minority groups. Its large segment of
Chinese are divided in loyalties between
Nationalist and Communist China, and
there are political and religious differ
ences between virtually all factions.
Communist efforts to take over the PEN
insula have been unceasing for the past
decade and, by agreement, British troops
will remain to defend the new fedora
ton against Communist guerrilla forces.
Economically, the peninsula states are
rich In mineral resources and natural
rubber production amounts to about
one-third Of the world supply. This
economy, however, Is one that requires
investment and development.


Under the new Malayan constitu-
ton, there viii be an elected monarch"
chosen every five years from among
the rulers Of the original nine states. A
legislative body will consist Of a Senate
designated mostly by appointment
and House Of Representatives popu-
larry elected. The individual states will
retain considerable autonomy. Singa-
pore, the British Crown Colony at the
tip Of the peninsula, will remain in that
status for the time being but will have
close economic and communications ties
with the new federation.


In taking on its new status, Malaga
has passed significant milestone even
though its immediate course is an UNI
certain one.
